title: Engram control sidecars from earlier host instances survive TermAl restarts and are never reaped (two orphans from Oct 4 and 5 still running)
outcome: A host-started `engram control` sidecar never outlives the host instance that started it. On host exit or restart, its control children end with it (Windows Job object kill-on-close or equivalent), and a host that starts while orphans from an earlier instance remain finds and reports them without killing anything automatically, unless a safe rule says otherwise. The idle reap covers sidecars whose owning session is gone. A test covers host exit ending the sidecars, and the docs state the lifecycle.
acceptance: A TermAl-started Engram control sidecar is a member of a kill-on-close job from creation (atomic PROC_THREAD_ATTRIBUTE_JOB_LIST, or windows_launch's fresh-lease suspended fallback). There is no moment when it runs or waits outside that job; containment Unavailable is reported in the host log. A test shows the child is in the job before its first resume.

Every failure between creation and the first resume terminates and reaps the child. A fail-first test injects a failure right after creation and observes the process exit. Today it stays alive and suspended, so the test is RED on master.
Ending the host's hold on the job (the effect of host exit) ends a running sidecar. A test shows it with a real child process.
At startup the host finds Engram control processes left by an earlier host instance and reports them (pid, start time, session), killing nothing. A test covers the detection over a process snapshot.
docs state the sidecar lifecycle: start, containment, the idle reap, host exit and orphan reporting.
The full five-stage gate passes on the exact committed tree.
